full_judgment:
This Rule, on an application, under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 at the instance of the defendant-petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos.1-3 to show cause as to why the delay of 259 days in filing the revisional application against the judgment and decree dated 13-9-2012 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narail in Title Appeal No.91 of 2006 affirming the judgment and decree dated 5-6-2006 passed by the Assistant Judge, Kalia, Narail in Title Suit No.52 of 2004 decreeing the suit should not be condoned and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this. Court may seem fit and proper. 

 7. On going to the materials on record it is found that the Rule was issued for condonation of 259 days delay in preferring the revision. The defendant-petitioners narrated the reasons for delay in paragraph No.2 of his petition from where it is found that the judgment and decree was pronounced by the appellate Court below on 13-9-2012 and the defendant-petitioners obtained the certified copy of the same on 18-10-2012 but thereafter since they have been living in the remote area of Kalia Upazila under Narail district they could not come at Narail town in time and they did not know about the law of limitation, as such, there appears mainly two grounds for con- donation of delay that they have been living in the remote area of Kalia Upazila and the ignorance of law by them. 

 9. So far the second ground is concerned that they were not aware about the law of limitation but ignorance of law is no excuse at all. 

 10. In the law of limitation there is no any prescribed time limit for filing of the civil revision in this Court but it is the long standing practice of this Court that the time schedule for filing of the appeal in this Court is considered as the time schedule for filing of the civil revision and it is also settled principle that in appropriate case this Court can entertain the civil revision where there appears no intentional negligence on the part of the petitioners in filing the revision. 

 "It appears that the explanation given for the delay of 309 days in the application for condonation of delay is merely in the nature of a general explanation and not on day-to-day basis and, as such, it is not a sufficient explanation within the meaning as contemplated in section 5 of the Limitation Act. It appears from the application that the reason for the delay was narrated and explained in a very slipshod general manner giving rise to form the opinion that the delay was due to the laches and gross negligence on the part of the petitioner. I do not find any substance in the Rule."
